analysis: The only change is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md: head lines 498-507 add a "Prompt preparation and admission" table with DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _MB, _VERIFY, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE. The two supplied units end at line 486, so the added lines are visible only in the truncated patch excerpt. I read the rest of the file for context and found no other security-relevant changes. No code changed, so no control was weakened. The new rows describe a provider-side token-ID cache for rendered chat-template pieces, keyed by the request's prefix-cache scope. It is read at tokenizer load and the LaunchAgent forwards it. A global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE disable also turns it off. Open questions for integration: (1) T-041/SEC-035 covers prefix-cache sharing and the TTFT timing oracle. A new in-memory cache of prompt-derived pieces with LRU storage of up to 4096 MiB could extend the same-account hit/miss timing channel. The doc says the cache is scoped per prefix-cache scope, which is coordinator-authored from account, model build and prompt contract. PromptTokenCache.swift was not supplied, so whether this isolation holds is unverified. (2) The cached data lives in provider process memory, which is already in the T-011/T-014 operator-memory exposure class, and it is not documented as written to disk. (3) The verify and template-loop rewrite paths claim identical token IDs and fall back on mismatch. That is a correctness claim, not an attestation or secrecy control (T-056). The T-041 threat model could add a note that the prompt token cache is a scope-keyed, in-memory, per-tokenizer cache, but nothing here shows a regression. The implementation needs deeper review.
